meta.title: FLEXIDATA | Edge data centres as flexibility resources for the power grid
meta.description: Research and innovation project funded by the Italian Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security to enable edge data centres to provide flexibility to the power grid and cut their emissions.

banner.funded_by: Project funded by the Italian Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security (MASE)
banner.call: Public Call under Art. 4(1) of Ministerial Decree No. 386/2023
banner.area: Strategic area: Flexibility and energy storage

hero.title: Decarbonising data centres: a strategic opportunity to build an Italian flexibility backbone supporting the power grid
hero.subtitle: Edge data centres, from passive consumers to active resources for the power grid.

concept.title: The concept
concept.c1_text: The growth of renewables and new electrical loads makes the ability to modulate consumption close to grid stress points increasingly valuable.
concept.c2_title: Edge data centres are already distributed
concept.c2_text: They are spread across the territory, run computing loads that can partly be deferred or relocated, and host local assets such as cooling, solar PV and storage.
concept.c3_text: IT workload orchestration, asset management and aggregation turn the ability to modulate and to improve efficiency into value for the grid and for site operators.

arch.title: Platform architecture
arch.intro: From the field to the grid operator: select a block to see its function, inputs and outputs.

field.title: Field
field.outputs: Power metered at the POD, IT load, cooling, solar PV, storage, environmental data

twin.title: Digital twin
twin.function: Represents the site by combining BIM models and sensor data.

simulator.title: Simulator
simulator.function: Generates consumption profiles, available-flexibility estimates and asset configuration scenarios for each node.
simulator.inputs: Site state, weather and load forecasts, asset configuration
simulator.outputs: Expected profiles, available flexibility per interval, scenarios

orchestrator.title: Orchestrator
orchestrator.function: Decides where and when to run IT workloads and how to modulate local assets, within service-level constraints (SLAs).
orchestrator.inputs: Available flexibility, price signal, SLA constraints, modulation requests

aggregator.title: Aggregation platform
aggregator.function: Aggregates node flexibility at portfolio level, values it and offers it.
aggregator.outputs: Flexibility offers, outcomes, requests to the orchestrator

grid.title: Grid operator
grid.function: Requests power modulation within defined time windows.

arch.price_dispatch: Price as a spatio-temporal dispatch signal
arch.price_valuation: Price as an economic valuation input
arch.price_note: The same price signal plays two distinct roles: it drives the orchestrator's decisions and, separately, the valuation of flexibility in the aggregation platform.

sim.title: Simulator
sim.intro: Two modes, the same tools: providing flexibility or improving the efficiency of site assets.

flex.tolerance_note: Illustrative delivery tolerance: {pct}% of the requested quantity per interval.
flex.definition_flex: Flexibility = baseline minus power metered at the POD, net of cooling, solar PV and storage.

eff.strategy_unavailable: Strategy not included in this version of the data.
eff.sizes: Simulated sizes: PV {pv} kWp, storage {kwh} kWh / {kw} kW

tooltip.self_consumption: Share of solar PV generation consumed on site.
tooltip.self_sufficiency: Share of site demand covered by local generation.
tooltip.pue: Ratio of total site energy to IT energy. It does not change when PV or storage is installed.
tooltip.cue: CO₂ emissions associated with grid import per kWh of IT energy.

eff.bess_idle: At this node solar PV generation never exceeds the load: there is no surplus to store and storage in self-consumption mode stays idle. Try the peak shaving strategy.
eff.bridge_conflict: Storage capacity reserved for flexibility is not available for self-consumption, and vice versa.
eff.baseline_note: Installing solar PV and storage changes the baseline at the POD: flexibility is always calculated against the active asset configuration.
eff.econ_note: Illustrative, editable values. They are not a project estimate.

E1.note: Spatial shift accepted: positive economic balance, latency and capacity at the receiving node within constraints.

E2.note: Spatial shift rejected: insufficient IT capacity at the receiving node and negative balance. Only local levers remain, partial delivery.

E3.note: Spatial shift accepted, combined with workload deferral and cooling.

map.title: The node network
map.intro: When a node receives a modulation request, part of the computing load can run at another node.

tooltip.title: Economic test of the shift
tooltip.src_energy: Energy avoided at the source node
tooltip.dst_energy: Additional energy at the destination node
tooltip.dst_price: Effective price at the destination node
tooltip.rule: The shift pays off only if the balance is positive and service constraints (latency, capacity) are met.

temporal.title: Temporal load shifting
temporal.principle: Deferrable computing workloads are brought forward or postponed relative to the requested window.
temporal.constraints: Job deadlines, load rebound after the window

spatial.title: Spatial shifting between nodes
spatial.principle: Part of the computing load runs at a node located in another area of the grid.
spatial.constraints: Latency, receiving-node capacity, differential economic benefit

bess.title: Battery storage
bess.principle: Charging and discharging to move energy in time, shave peaks or provide flexibility.
bess.constraints: Power, capacity, state of charge, degradation

hvac.title: Thermal inertia and cooling
hvac.principle: Pre-cooling and setpoint modulation exploiting the thermal inertia of the rooms.

pv.title: Solar PV
pv.principle: Local generation reduces grid import and the associated emissions.
